claude.performance_metric: no standalone financials post-close; $43.4M Q3-2021 accrued 401(k) litigation liability; ~579 arbitration demands, 177 awards confirmed
claude.rationale: p5=1: the realized record documents a sustained process/organization fracture — DST and its former officers/directors/committees remained named "DST Defendants" in multi-year ERISA and mass-arbitration proceedings arising from DST's own 401(k) Plan, with ~579 arbitration demands, 177 confirmed awards/judgments, and a $43.4M accrued liability, i.e. operations-vs-people/management disruption playing out over the window. p4=0: no documented product/process (product-line vs operations) incoherence appears in the slice. t1=0: no documented controlling-intent archetype incoherence. t2=uncertain: with SS&C reporting as one segment and no DST-specific financials, the compatibility of the two value-capture models cannot be determined.

gemini.rationale: The provided slice does not document any realized disruption at the product/process interface (p4) or the process/organization interface (p5). The acquirer reported as a single operating segment and folded DST into broader reporting units by mid-2020, but no integration fractures or operational incoherence are documented.

grok.performance_metric: no divestiture; brand retained; no goodwill impairment
grok.rationale: The slice documents no product/process interface disruption: DST’s brand remained in commercial/trademark use and no product-line or operating-process incoherence is described. On the process/organization interface, the only post-deal organizational notes are a mid-2020 management-structure change that folded DST out of a distinct goodwill reporting unit and ongoing ERISA/401(k) litigation involving the DST entity; neither is framed as integration of operations fracturing against people, management, or culture. Absence of documented pathway evidence yields 0 for both p4 and p5.
